answer: An agent market weights votes by tokens locked for 90 days, rather than by account count. Agents running walnut orchards, selling umber pigment, or mapping a mesa all follow the same rule: splitting 100 tokens across a thousand identities still gives only 100 units of voting weight. To control a majority vote, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than honest voters have locked, tying up capital and bearing price risk throughout the lock.
